stories.delivered_paragraph: Rescuers were searching for 15 hikers feared missing after flash flooding struck the Grand Canyon, turning what one survivor described as a beautiful day into a scene of people screaming. The hiker was airlifted to safety, but the available reporting did not specify where the missing group was last seen or whether anyone had been found. The incident underscores how quickly canyon storms can isolate visitors and complicate rescue operations.

stories.delivered_paragraph: U.S. forces struck two Iranian launchers on Larak Island after observing Revolutionary Guard personnel preparing rockets with sea mines for the Strait of Hormuz, U.S. Central Command said. Iran said the attack killed and wounded several personnel and claimed retaliation against U.S. targets in Jordan; Jordan said it intercepted eight missiles. Brent crude rose 1.54% to $89.46 a barrel as the first publicly acknowledged U.S. strike inside Iran since late July renewed fears for shipping through the key energy route.

stories.delivered_paragraph: ESPN’s Michael Florio identified 15 potential fantasy-football “league winners” for 2026—players whose production could far exceed their draft cost and help decide championships. Among them is quarterback Jaxson Dart, who averaged 20.13 fantasy points in 12 starts last season, the fifth-highest rookie-quarterback average ever, according to the analysis. The central draft question is whether managers can find that kind of late or middle-round value before it becomes obvious to the rest of their league.

stories.delivered_paragraph: The SEC will for now comply with a Louisiana judge’s temporary order blocking punishment of schools that use athletes who return after signing professional contracts, but plans to challenge it at a Thursday hearing. The conference’s new rule would penalize a school with measures including a coach’s half-season suspension and a fine equal to 50% of the sport’s annual budget. The case could determine how far conferences can go in regulating athletes’ increasingly fluid paths between college and pro sports.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Paramount Games Studio is considering games based on Taylor Sheridan properties including Yellowstone and Lioness while building a video-game division around major company franchises, Polygon reported. Its first announced project is an adaptation of Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: The Last Ronin with PlatinumGames, developer of Bayonetta; the studio says its core targets also include Star Trek and Avatar: The Last Airbender. The strategy would extend Paramount’s TV and film brands into a business built on long-running, recognizable worlds.

stories.delivered_paragraph: The 90-minute action thriller Quentin Tarantino has called “my favorite” is now available free on streaming, Polygon reported. The report frames it as holiday horror, a genre turning celebrations such as Valentine’s Day into settings for violence and suspense rather than romance. Free availability gives a cult-style film a wider route to viewers as streaming services increasingly use older genre titles to draw audiences without a rental charge.

stories.delivered_paragraph: An anonymous Emmy-winning TV Academy producer offered sharply negative assessments of several contenders in a Hollywood Reporter “brutally honest” ballot, while calling Widow’s Bay “far and away the best” comedy on television. The voter dismissed DTF St. Louis, criticized Your Friends and Neighbors as about entitled people, and said stereotypes in Nobody Wants This were uncomfortable. The comments are one voter’s opinion but illustrate how subjective and divided awards-season judgments can be before ballots are counted.

stories.delivered_paragraph: U.S. stock-index futures slipped Sunday after comments by Kevin Warsh at Jackson Hole led investors to reassess the chance of another interest-rate increase. Markets were also looking ahead to labor data and technology-company earnings later this week, both of which could reshape expectations for growth and monetary policy. Higher-rate fears matter because they raise borrowing costs and can weigh especially heavily on stock valuations, leaving investors focused on whether incoming data validate the market’s repricing.
